id.description: The team's prefix and the next free number, such as ISS-014. Never reused.

title.description: What is wrong or wanted, in one short line.

type.description: bug: behaviour is wrong. feature: a new capability. improvement: a better existing one. task: bounded work with no feature claim.

status.description: Where the issue is, in workflow order. done and cancelled are closed.

priority.description: Scheduling urgency: p0 urgent, p1 high, p2 normal, p3 low.

severity.description: For bugs: how bad the impact is. Not the same as priority.

assignee.description: Who is doing it: a link to their record ([[people/ana-ruiz]]) when the team has a people directory, otherwise their name.

reporter.description: Who reported it, as a link or a name.

labels.description: Short lowercase areas such as auth or billing.

parent.description: The larger issue this is part of, as a link.

related_to.description: Related issues, as links. Add the link on both issues.

blocked_by.description: Issues that must be done first, as links. The other issue lists this one in blocks.

blocks.description: Issues waiting on this one, as links. The other issue lists this one in blocked_by.

due_at.description: When it must be done, if there is a real date.

created_at.description: When it was filed, in UTC. Kept on every update.

source_paths.description: Where the report came from: links to pages or records, URLs, or a short note.

content.description: The problem, evidence, acceptance criteria and discussion, in Markdown. Don't repeat the fields.
